originalTitle: Trump renews bid to fire Fed governor Lisa Cook despite supreme court ruling
summary: White House continues to target Cook despite decision from justices that upheld Federal Reserve’s independence
content: Donald Trump is attempting once again to oust the US Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook over allegations of mortgage fraud, despite a recent US supreme court decision that upheld the central bank’s independence. Cook reportedly received a letter from the White House this week that provided notice, in accordance to the supreme court’s June ruling, that Trump was “considering removing” her from her Fed position over the same claims of mortgage fraud that he levied against her last summer. The letter, first reported by ABC News, accused Cook of falling “well short of the standard” required of a sitting Fed governor and requested she provide a written response to the allegations within three weeks. The supreme court in June ruled 5-4 that Cook was entitled to stay on as Fed governor while she fights the president’s allegations, writing in its majority opinion that Trump “failed to afford Cook the procedural protections to which she was entitled by statute”. “Without such protections, she could not properly dispute the charges the president laid against her,” the justices said. In response to the White House’s letter, one of Cook’s lawyers, Abbe D Lowell, called the allegations “as baseless now as they were a year ago when President Trump tried to remove Governor Cook and interfere with the independence of the Federal Reserve”. “No matter what President Trump tries to do next, this much is clear under the facts and Supreme Court precedent – there is no valid cause for removing Governor Cook,” Lowell said in a statement. “As we did before, we will challenge this latest pretext and preserve her position and the historic role of the Fed.” The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Cook was appointed by Joe Biden in 2022 to a 14-year term that will end in 2038. She is the first Black woman to serve as a Fed governor. Before she joined the Fed, she served on Barack Obama’s council of economic advisers and has taught at Harvard University and Stanford University. Trump first abruptly fired Cook last August in an unprecedented attack on the central bank’s independence. The White House accused her of wrongly designating two separate properties in Georgia and Michigan as her primary residence and failing to report rental income on her Atlanta property for two years. Cook denied the allegations and sued the Trump administration for firing her without cause or proper procedure. Cook and her legal team have maintained that the claims of mortgage fraud are based on “inadvertent” paperwork errors and that the administration is “cherrypicking” facts. Cook’s firing and ongoing legal battles also coincided with Trump’s attacks on the Fed for not lowering rates. Cook, along with then Fed chair, Jerome Powell, had backed the central bank’s decision not to lower rates, which drew the ire of the White House. Trump called Powell “too stupid and too political” and launched a justice department investigation into his renovations of the Fed’s headquarters in Washington, which has since been dropped. The Fed is now under the leadership of Kevin Warsh, a Trump pick who had previously shown favor towards cutting rates. Warsh has maintained that he will make decisions based on economic data, not the will of the president, and has made it his mission to fight the country’s heightened inflation, which typically is addressed by rate hikes. “We’re an independent central bank,” he said in response to questioning from Democratic House members at a hearing in July. “We’re honored to be independent.”
chineseTitle: 尽管最高法院做出裁决，特朗普仍再次提出解雇美联储理事丽莎·库克的提议
chineseSummary: 尽管法官做出了维护美联储独立性的决定，但白宫仍继续针对库克
chineseContent: 尽管美国最高法院最近裁决维持了美联储的独立性，但唐纳德·特朗普仍试图因抵押贷款欺诈指控而再次罢免美联储理事丽莎·库克。据报道，库克本周收到了一封来自白宫的信函，根据最高法院 6 月份的裁决，特朗普正在“考虑解除”她的美联储职务，理由是他去年夏天对她提出的抵押贷款欺诈指控。这封信首先由美国广播公司新闻报道，指责库克“远远没有达到现任美联储理事的标准”，并要求她在三周内对这些指控做出书面回应。最高法院6月以5比4裁定库克有权在她与总统的指控作斗争时继续担任美联储理事，并在多数意见中写道，特朗普“未能向库克提供她依法享有的程序保护”。法官们表示：“如果没有这样的保护，她就无法对总统对她提出的指控提出合理的质疑。”库克的律师阿贝·D·洛厄尔(Abbe D Lowell)在回应白宫的信函时称，这些指控“现在与一年前特朗普总统试图罢免库克州长并干涉美联储独立性时一样毫无根据”。洛厄尔在一份声明中表示：“无论特朗普总统下一步试图做什么，根据事实和最高法院的先例，这一点是显而易见的——没有正当理由罢免库克州长。” “就像我们之前所做的那样，我们将挑战这一最新借口，并维护她的地位和美联储的历史性作用。”白宫没有立即回应置评请求。库克于 2022 年由乔·拜登任命，任期 14 年，任期将于 2022 年结束
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
